content:
# Sirach 32 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** SIR 032 | **Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Total Disagreements:** 15

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "master of the feast" vs. "in charge of a dinner party"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "master of the feast" (preserves symposiarch role)
- **PNEUMA:** "put in charge of a dinner party"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "master of the feast" — the Hellenistic symposiarch role is specific and should be preserved; PNEUMA's version is functional but loses the cultural register.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.1b: "be lifted up" vs. "exalt yourself"

- **EMET:** "do not be lifted up"
- **LOGOS:** "do not exalt yourself"
- **PNEUMA:** "Don't let it go to your head"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Do not exalt yourself" — active voice matches the imperative series; PNEUMA's idiom is lively but too colloquial.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.2: "garland" vs. "crown"

- **EMET:** "receive a garland for your proper conduct"
- **LOGOS:** "receive a crown for your good management"
- **PNEUMA:** "the honor that comes with doing it well"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "garland" — more specific to the banquet context (symposium victory wreaths); LOGOS's "crown" implies royal dignity; PNEUMA loses the concrete image.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.3: "for it is fitting for you" vs. "for it is your right"

- **EMET:** "it is fitting for you"
- **LOGOS:** "it is your right"
- **PNEUMA:** "that's your prerogative"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "it is fitting for you" — πρέπει σοι is about propriety, not legal right; LOGOS and PNEUMA both shift toward entitlement.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.5: gemstone identification

- **EMET:** "ruby seal on a necklace of gold"
- **LOGOS:** "ruby seal on a setting of gold"
- **PNEUMA:** "ruby set in gold"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "ruby seal on a setting of gold" (LOGOS) — "seal" preserves the σφραγίς meaning; "necklace" (EMET) is an over-specification.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.7: conditions for speaking

- **EMET:** "only if there is need, yet no more than twice and only if asked"
- **LOGOS:** "if you must, yet scarcely, and only when you are asked twice"
- **PNEUMA:** "only when you must — and even then, briefly, only when you've been asked more than once"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "only if you must — yet scarcely, and only when asked more than once" — combines precision with natural phrasing.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.8: "be brief" vs. "speak concisely"

- **EMET:** "Be brief, say much in few words"
- **LOGOS:** "Speak concisely; say much in few words"
- **PNEUMA:** "Get to the point"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Be concise; say much in few words" — combines EMET/LOGOS; PNEUMA loses the aphoristic quality.

---

## Disagreement 8 — v.10: character before speech

- **EMET:** "before a modest man grace goes before him"
- **LOGOS:** "before a man of genuine character grace goes before him"
- **PNEUMA:** "a person of genuine character makes a good impression before they even open their mouth"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "before a man of genuine character, grace goes before him" — LOGOS identifies the referent well; PNEUMA's paraphrase is accurate but destroys the aphoristic parallelism.

---

## Disagreement 9 — v.11: "rise betimes" vs. "rise at the right time"

- **EMET:** "Rise betimes and do not be last"
- **LOGOS:** "Rise at the right time and do not be the last"
- **PNEUMA:** "Leave in good time; don't be the last to go"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Rise at the right time and do not be the last" — "betimes" (EMET) is archaic; PNEUMA changes "rise" to "leave," which is a possible reading but less literal.

---

## Disagreement 10 — v.12b: "proud speech" vs. "arrogant"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "through proud speech"
- **PNEUMA:** "let your speech become arrogant"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "through proud speech" — preserves Ben Sira's repeated theme of pride; PNEUMA's phrasing is accurate but less pointed.

---

## Disagreement 11 — v.13: "filled you" vs. "intoxicates you"

- **EMET:** "who has filled you with his good things"
- **LOGOS:** "who intoxicates you with his good things"
- **PNEUMA:** "who has lavished his good things upon you"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "who fills you with his good things" — LOGOS's "intoxicates" is a playful reading given the banquet context but goes too far; PNEUMA's "lavished" is a good supplement but alters the image.

---

## Disagreement 12 — v.15: "filled by it" vs. "enriched by it"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "will be filled by it"
- **PNEUMA:** "will be enriched by it"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "will be filled by it" — the Greek ἐμπλησθήσεται ("filled") should be preserved; PNEUMA's "enriched" is too vague.

---

## Disagreement 13 — v.17: "shuns reproof" vs. "resents correction"

- **EMET:** "shuns reproof"
- **LOGOS:** "turns aside reproof"
- **PNEUMA:** "resents correction"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "shuns reproof" — ἐκκλίνει suggests avoidance; PNEUMA's "resents" implies the opposite (feels it but pushes back) rather than avoidance.

---

## Disagreement 14 — v.19: "do not regret it" vs. "do not be plagued by regret"

- **EMET:** "do not regret it"
- **LOGOS:** "do not regret your actions after the fact"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't second-guess yourself"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "do not be plagued by regret" — a deliberate choice completed should not generate ongoing second-guessing; this emphasizes the quality of the deliberation.

---

## Disagreement 15 — v.24: "delivered" vs. "rescued"

- **EMET:** "he will be delivered again and again"
- **LOGOS:** "God will rescue him again and again"
- **PNEUMA:** "God will rescue them time and again"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "he will be rescued again and again" — passive preserves ambiguity; the repetition "again and again" is kept from all versions.
